intro.title: Cart Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart feature for an e-commerce app using React's Context API. You will learn how to create a centralized Cart Context to manage cart state, such as items and totals, and make it accessible across multiple components without prop drilling. The core programming concept involves using React's useContext hook and Context.Provider to share state globally within your application. By the end, you will have a functional cart that can add items, update quantities, and calculate the total price, all managed through a clean, reusable context structure.
intro.usecase: Cart Context is essential for e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, where shopping cart data must be accessible across multiple components—product listings, cart summaries, checkout pages, and header badges. This pattern allows users to add items from product cards while instantly updating the cart total in a sidebar panel, without prop drilling through intermediate components. Developers implement Cart Context to maintain consistent state across complex UI flows, ensuring cart persistence during navigation and enabling features like saved-for-later items or multi-step checkout processes.
